title: Micro-organisms
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Micro-organisms Worksheets (Bacteria, Yeast and Mould)
standard_code: Year 6: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Describe how living things are classified into broad groups according to common observable characteristics and based on similarities and differences, including micro-organisms, plants and animals.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on micro-organisms: bacteria, yeast and mould, helpful and harmful microbes, mould and yeast investigations and stopping germs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Tiny living things: helpful and harmful.
key_sub: Bacteria and fungi are too small to see, but they make bread, yoghurt and illness.
body_html:
How to think about it

Micro-organisms are living things too small to see without a microscope.

  • Bacteria and fungi (such as yeast and moulds) are micro-organisms. Viruses are germs that cause illness.
  • Helpful: yeast makes bread rise, bacteria make yoghurt, decomposers recycle dead things, mould gave us penicillin.
  • Harmful: bacteria cause food poisoning and tooth decay; moulds spoil food. Washing hands, cooking food and cold storage help.
Example

Bread in a fridge or a warm cupboard: which goes mouldy first?

Mould grows faster when warm

Answer: the warm cupboard

Example

A bacterium is 2 µm long. How many across 1 mm?

1 mm = 1,000 µm

1,000 ÷ 2

Answer: 500

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all micro-organisms are harmful.
  • Thinking the fridge kills bacteria (it only slows them down).
  • Thinking yeast works best in very hot water.

faq.a: Living things that are too small to see with the naked eye, such as bacteria and some fungi (yeast and moulds). You need a microscope to see them.
Both. Yeast makes bread rise, bacteria make yoghurt and decomposers recycle nutrients, but some bacteria cause food poisoning and moulds spoil food.

faq.q: Why does food last longer in the fridge?
faq.a: Cold slows down the growth of bacteria and moulds. It does not kill them, so food still goes off in time.

items.q: Which kind of micro-organism is linked to food poisoning from undercooked chicken?
items.e: Food poisoning from undercooked chicken: bacteria. (Yeast and moulds are both fungi.)

items.q: Which kind of micro-organism is linked to colds and flu?
items.e: Colds and flu: viruses. (Yeast and moulds are both fungi.)

items.q: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
items.e: He noticed mould killing bacteria on a dish.
